name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is the Maven integration adapter for Machai Ghostwriter. It brings Guided File Processing and AI-assisted project maintenance into Maven builds: guidance embedded in project files directs repeatable processing of source code, tests, documentation, site content, configuration, and other selected files. The plugin provides aggregator goals that can work across a Maven reactor or without a pom.xml, per-module goals that use Maven reactor scheduling, and act execution for reusable named acts or direct prompts. It resolves Maven project, session, reactor, and settings context; selects paths and exclusions; forwards model and instruction settings; can obtain provider credentials and custom provider configuration from Maven settings.xml; and registers Java class-discovery and reflection tools when a Maven project is available. Its main value is making AI-assisted documentation and project workflow automation reproducible, Maven-aware, configurable, and suitable for multi-module builds.

features.name: gw:gw
features.description: Runs the thread-safe aggregator guidance workflow. It scans selected files for Ghostwriter guidance comments and processes them with the configured AI provider. It can run in a Maven project, coordinate a multi-module build, or run without a pom.xml; when it coordinates modules, submodules are processed before parent modules.

examples.description: Step 1: add the plugin to the Maven build. Step 2: configure a matching my-ai-provider server in Maven settings.xml with provider credentials. Step 3: run the guidance goal from the project root to process guidance-tagged files below src while skipping generated and dependency directories.

features.name: gw:act
features.description: Runs a Ghostwriter act as a thread-safe aggregator. The gw.act value may name a predefined act, add instructions after an act name, or begin with > for a prompt-only action. The goal supports selected paths, model and instruction overrides, exclusions, custom act locations, Maven settings credentials, and reverse-order module processing.

examples.description: Step 1: configure provider credentials under my-ai-provider in Maven settings.xml. Step 2: invoke the installed plugin with a prompt-only act; the leading > prevents the text from being interpreted as a predefined act name. Step 3: limit processing to site documentation and disable prompting for automation.

features.name: gw:gw-per-module
features.description: Runs guidance processing once for every module in the active Maven reactor. Maven determines module order using its normal dependency graph. This goal requires a Maven project and reuses the shared provider, scan, and class-introspection configuration.

examples.description: Run this command from a multi-module reactor after configuring the plugin and provider. Each module processes its own site directory according to Maven reactor order, using shared instructions and exclusions.

features.name: gw:act-per-module
features.description: Runs an act in the standard Maven reactor context for Maven projects. It inherits act, model, path, instruction, exclusion, interactive, and Maven settings configuration from the aggregator act implementation.

examples.description: After installing and configuring the plugin and server id, run a prompt-only act for each applicable reactor module. The command targets the module site content and obtains credentials from Maven settings.xml.

features.name: find_class and get_class_info
features.signature: java.util.List<java.lang.String> findClass(java.lang.String className, java.io.File projectDir); java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> getClassInfo(java.lang.String className, java.io.File projectDir) throws java.lang.ClassNotFoundException
features.description: Provides Ghostwriter function tools for Maven-project-aware Java discovery and reflection. find_class matches a regular expression against simple class names and returns fully qualified names. get_class_info returns metadata for a fully qualified class, including modifiers, hierarchy, non-private fields and methods, constructors, annotations, origin path, dependency coordinates, and matching project source path when available.

examples.description: In an AI workflow started through the configured Maven plugin, first call find_class with a simple-name regular expression to discover candidates. Then pass a selected fully qualified name to get_class_info to inspect the accessible API and its source or artifact origin.

customizations.name: Maven properties and plugin configuration
customizations.description: Configure gw.model, gw.path, gw.instructions, gw.excludes, genai.serverId, gw.config, gw.act, gw.acts, and gw.interactive through Maven command-line properties or plugin configuration. A Maven settings.xml server selected by genai.serverId can provide provider username, password, and custom XML configuration values.

examples.description: Enable focused SLF4J SimpleLogger diagnostics for the Maven adapter while scanning src. Replace the fully qualified logger name and level as required.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run guided processing
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.3.0 to the build plugins section.
Create a Maven settings.xml server entry containing the selected GenAI provider credentials and use its id as genai.serverId.
Place Ghostwriter guidance comments in project files that describe the desired maintenance work.
Run mvn gw:gw -Dgw.path=src -Dgenai.serverId=my-ai-provider and review the resulting changes.
Build and test the project before committing guidance and generated updates.

examples.title: Run a direct documentation-maintenance scenario
steps: Install the plugin in the Maven build and configure a provider server in settings.xml.
Run mvn gw:act '-Dgw.act=>Update the project documentation' -Dgw.path=src/site -Dgenai.serverId=my-ai-provider -Dgw.interactive=false.
Review generated Markdown or site changes, then run the normal Maven verification lifecycle.
